NXEON DESIGN SYSTEM — POLISH PASS
Phase 2 continuation. Do not start Phase 3.

==================================================
CONTEXT — READ THIS FIRST
==================================================

Phase 2 (the Nxeon design system) was already built by a prior session at
/opt/nxeon-designsystem. It is a complete, isolated Next.js app: design tokens,
a 60-icon family, four surface archetypes (object/container/plate/rule), a
full component library, a canvas-based rotating globe, five per-product
deployment loaders, and a showcase route at /design that documents all of it.

Before touching anything, read these three files in full:
  1. /opt/nxeon-designsystem/README.md
  2. /root/.claude/projects/-root/memory/nxeon-design-system-phase2.md
  3. /root/.claude/projects/-root/memory/nxeon-brand-gradient.md
Also check the memory index at /root/.claude/projects/-root/memory/MEMORY.md
for any other nxeon-* entries relevant to this project (there is one about a
past pkill incident — read it, it matters for the safety rules below).

Do NOT trust memory files over the actual code. If something in memory
disagrees with what you find in the repo, the repo is the truth — the
memory may be stale or describe something that was later changed.

This is NOT a rebuild. The system, the tokens, the four surface archetypes,
the icon set, the globe, the deploy loaders and the component library are
all APPROVED. Your job is to tighten what exists, not redesign it.

==================================================
CRITICAL: ISOLATION AND PRODUCTION SAFETY
==================================================

/opt/nxeon-designsystem is a from-scratch, isolated project — no .env file,
no database client, no payment/registrar/mail/hypervisor SDK, no fetch() to
anything, zero runtime dependencies beyond next/react/react-dom. Keep it
that way. Do not add a backend call, an environment variable, or any
dependency that talks to a real service.

DO NOT touch /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging, or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. Those are
the real production, staging, and an older sandbox tree. Read-only if you
need to reference something (e.g. a token you're unsure about), never write.

The sandbox runs as a manually started process on port 3010 (not systemd,
not in nginx's main config). It is reverse-proxied for review at:
  https://flow.k9x4rq7wpz2ah6t.nxeon.cloud/ds/design
via a `location /ds/` block added to the EXISTING nxeon-sandbox nginx vhost,
protected by basic auth. Credentials: user "nxeon", password in
/root/.ds-review-password (read it, don't ask the owner to repeat it).
Do not touch nginx config or that vhost. If the app on :3010 isn't running,
restart it yourself with `cd /opt/nxeon-designsystem && npx next start -p 3010`
run detached (setsid nohup ... &).

NEVER kill processes by a generic command-line pattern (no `pkill -f "next"`,
no `pkill -f "next start"`, no `killall node`). Every Node service on this
host — prod, staging, this sandbox — shares similar command lines, and a
pattern match has taken production down before. To stop only this sandbox,
find its PID by the port it's bound to and kill that PID specifically:
  PID=$(ss -ltnpH 'sport = :3010' | grep -oP 'pid=\K[0-9]+' | head -1)
  [ -n "$PID" ] && kill "$PID"
Verify production is unaffected after any restart:
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3000/
  (expect 200 — that's the real production app, do not disturb it)

==================================================
WHAT "POLISH" MEANS HERE
==================================================

Go through the whole system with a fine comb. Concretely:

make some of the motion graphics better, more premium effects, styling, effects. use icons for the deploy wizard, creating reassurance cards with 30-day money back, 24/7 customer support, etc. Just improve on the foundation we already have here, think multimillion dollar ai start up company, not just some vibecoded app that feels generic

1. CONSISTENCY AUDIT
   - Every `.nx-object` usage: confirm the notch (chamfer) renders correctly
     with a real border along the diagonal, not a clipped-off edge. Check
     every place the pattern is used (checkout plan cards, game cards,
     inventory rows, region cards) at multiple widths — a rushed addition
     may have gotten the clip-path direction or size wrong somewhere.
   - Glow discipline: the rule is "at most one glow per surface" (nx-glow-soft
     / nx-glow-card / nx-glow-hero / nx-lift). Audit every page in app/design/
     and flag/fix any surface that stacks two, or where a glow was added
     without a clear reason.
   - Colour discipline: grep the whole components/ and app/ tree for any raw
     hex, rgb(), or arbitrary Tailwind colour value that isn't a token
     reference. There should be none in components; a couple in globals.css
     are expected (that's where tokens are defined) — everywhere else is a
     violation to fix.
   - Typography discipline: grep for arbitrary text-[...] sizes outside the
     defined scale (display/h1-h4/body/body-sm/caption/label/code/metric).
     Flag anything that snuck in.
   - KNOWN INCONSISTENCY TO FIX: the two-stage checkout pattern
     (app/design/patterns.tsx, Checkout function) still uses the flat SVG
     RegionMap component for its region step, while the dedicated "Region
     selector" showcase page (app/design/showpieces.tsx, Regions function)
     uses the much better Globe component. Decide whether checkout should
     use a compact version of the Globe instead for consistency, or whether
     RegionMap is deliberately the "inline/compact" variant and Globe is
     the "hero" variant — either is defensible, but make it a considered
     decision and document which, not an oversight.

2. ACCESSIBILITY RE-VERIFICATION
   A lot of visual work (glows, gradients, neon) landed fast late in the
   build and was not re-checked against the accessibility bar the tokens
   were originally built to hit. Re-verify:
   - Contrast of white text sitting on the brand gradient (e.g. the
     "Popular"/"Recommended" badges, the deploy button label) at actual
     rendered sizes — gradients can dip below AA at some points along the
     ramp even if the endpoints are fine.
   - That focus rings are still visibly distinguishable on surfaces that
     now carry a glow shadow (the glow and the focus ring can visually
     compete or the ring can get lost).
   - That every new animation added late (globe rotation, deploy loader
     loops, the sweep/trace effects) is actually caught by the global
     `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule in globals.css — trace it
     through, don't assume.
   - Re-run the label/association check on any new form-like controls
     added in the later patches (game picker, region cards) — confirm
     they're real buttons with aria-pressed, not divs with onClick.

3. PERFORMANCE
   - The globe (components/system/Globe.tsx) runs a requestAnimationFrame
     loop with ~20k points unconditionally, even when scrolled off-screen
     or on an inactive tab. Add an IntersectionObserver (or similar) to
     pause the rAF loop when the canvas isn't visible, and confirm
     document.visibilityState is respected too.
   - Check for any other unconditional animation loops with the same issue.
   - Run `npx next build` and confirm a clean production build: zero
     TypeScript errors, no new warnings introduced.

4. RESPONSIVE RE-CHECK
   Mobile (bottom nav, table-to-cards, bottom-sheet modals, sticky action
   bars, pinned checkout price) was the last thing built. Do a full sweep
   at 390px, 768px, and 1440px across every entry in the showcase sidebar
   and confirm: no horizontal overflow anywhere, the bottom nav's "More"
   drawer opens and traps focus correctly, and nothing added in the polish
   pass itself (e.g. a new glow or a wider hero) reintroduces overflow.

5. DENSITY
   Multiple pages (dashboard-style overview cards, some Container blocks)
   still read as airy/documentation-style rather than an infrastructure
   control surface. Tighten spacing and information density where it's
   clearly excessive — but don't fight the type scale or section-rule
   rhythm to do it; those are settled.

==================================================
HOW TO VERIFY YOUR WORK
==================================================

Use Playwright via the vendored chromium (same approach the prior session
used — check /opt/nxeon/node_modules/playwright-core and
/root/.cache/ms-playwright/ for the binary path) to screenshot every
sidebar entry at desktop (1440px), tablet (768px), and mobile (390px), and
actually look at the screenshots before claiming something is fixed.

After any code change: `npx next build` must succeed. Restart the dev
server on :3010 (port-specific kill only, see safety rules) and re-verify
the public review URL still returns 200 with auth
(`curl -u nxeon:$(cat /root/.ds-review-password) ...`) and 401 without it.

==================================================
WHAT NOT TO DO
==================================================

- Do not touch the magenta placeholder value (--color-brand-c in
  app/globals.css). It is intentionally a placeholder pending the owner's
  exact brand hex — read nxeon-brand-gradient.md before going anywhere
  near it. Do not guess a "better" value.
- Do not add new component categories or new pages to the showcase beyond
  what's needed to demonstrate a fix. This is a polish pass, not Phase 3.
- Do not migrate anything into the real /opt/nxeon portal. That is a later
  phase and requires separate owner approval.
- Do not add a git repo, CI config, or any tooling not already present
  unless it's directly needed to do the verification above.

==================================================
WHEN DONE
==================================================

Report: what you found in the consistency audit (with counts, like the
prior session's own findings — "N surfaces had a double glow", "N raw hex
values found"), what you fixed, the before/after on any a11y or perf issue,
and confirm the production build is clean and the review URL is live.
Do not start Phase 3.

(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

- baz: Create professional motion graphics and videos from the terminal. AI-powered composition with multi-track layering, choreography, voiceovers, and Lambda rendering. Gated 5-phase workflow ensures quality.
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.

# Nxeon Design System — Phase 2

The foundation for the portal redesign. Built from the approved Phase 1 blueprint.
**Isolated sandbox. Read `SANDBOX.md` before running anything.**

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3010/design
```

## What is here

| Layer | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens | `app/globals.css` | Colour, type, space, radius, elevation, glow, motion, z-index, focus, breakpoints |
| Icons | `components/system/Icon.tsx` | 60 icons, one geometry, three optical sizes |
| Surfaces + status | `components/system/primitives.tsx` | Object, Container, Plate, Rule, Badge, StatusIndicator, PageHeader, DataPlate, CopyButton |
| Controls | `components/system/controls.tsx` | Button, IconButton, Field, Input, Select, Textarea, Combobox, Toggle, Checkbox, Radio |
| Navigation | `components/system/navigation.tsx` | Tabs, SegmentedControl, Stepper, Progress, Wizard |
| Overlays | `components/system/overlays.tsx` | Modal, Drawer, ConfirmDialog, Dropdown, Tooltip, Alert, Toast |
| Data | `components/system/data.tsx` | Table, MetricTile, ResourceMeter, Sparkline, AreaChart |
| States | `components/system/states.tsx` | Loading, Empty, Error, Success, DeploymentLadder, SetupChecklist |
| Shell | `components/shell/AppShell.tsx` | Rail, top bar, content contract, mobile drawer |
| Showcase | `app/design/**` | The visual reference for every later phase |

## The rules this system enforces

1. **No raw values in components.** Colour, size, radius, duration and z-index all come from tokens.
   A phase-2 follow-up should add a lint rule so the build fails on a raw hex or an arbitrary font size.
2. **Four surface archetypes.** Object (notched, owns a filament), Container, Plate (technical data),
   Rule (labelled hairline). A border means "separate object" and is spent by role.
3. **One signal colour at a time.** Brand marks the single primary action; semantic colour marks state;
   violet is reserved for AI and Build.
4. **Nothing below 12px**, and 12px only for tracked uppercase labels.
5. **Every control is labelled.** `Field` produces the association; `IconButton` requires a label.
6. **Every overlay traps focus**, closes on Escape and restores focus on close.
7. **Reduced motion is off by default** and nothing opts back in.
8. **The ladder cannot lie.** `DeploymentLadder` takes named stages and has no percentage prop.

## Not in Phase 2

No product pages are migrated, no route is redesigned, and nothing connects to a backend.
That is Phase 3 and later.

  sign-off, so ask first.

# Nxeon Design System — Phase 2

The foundation for the portal redesign. Built from the approved Phase 1 blueprint.
**Isolated sandbox. Read `SANDBOX.md` before running anything.**

```bash
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:3010/design
```

## What is here

| Layer | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens | `app/globals.css` | Colour, type, space, radius, elevation, glow, motion, z-index, focus, breakpoints |
| Icons | `components/system/Icon.tsx` | 60 icons, one geometry, three optical sizes |
| Surfaces + status | `components/system/primitives.tsx` | Object, Container, Plate, Rule, Badge, StatusIndicator, PageHeader, DataPlate, CopyButton |
| Controls | `components/system/controls.tsx` | Button, IconButton, Field, Input, Select, Textarea, Combobox, Toggle, Checkbox, Radio |
| Navigation | `components/system/navigation.tsx` | Tabs, SegmentedControl, Stepper, Progress, Wizard |
| Overlays | `components/system/overlays.tsx` | Modal, Drawer, ConfirmDialog, Dropdown, Tooltip, Alert, Toast |
| Data | `components/system/data.tsx` | Table, MetricTile, ResourceMeter, Sparkline, AreaChart |
| States | `components/system/states.tsx` | Loading, Empty, Error, Success, DeploymentLadder, SetupChecklist |
| Shell | `components/shell/AppShell.tsx` | Rail, top bar, content contract, mobile drawer |
| Showcase | `app/design/**` | The visual reference for every later phase |

## The rules this system enforces

1. **No raw values in components.** Colour, size, radius, duration and z-index all come from tokens.
   A phase-2 follow-up should add a lint rule so the build fails on a raw hex or an arbitrary font size.
2. **Four surface archetypes.** Object (notched, owns a filament), Container, Plate (technical data),
   Rule (labelled hairline). A border means "separate object" and is spent by role.
3. **One signal colour at a time.** Brand marks the single primary action; semantic colour marks state;
   violet is reserved for AI and Build.
4. **Nothing below 12px**, and 12px only for tracked uppercase labels.
5. **Every control is labelled.** `Field` produces the association; `IconButton` requires a label.
6. **Every overlay traps focus**, closes on Escape and restores focus on close.
7. **Reduced motion is off by default** and nothing opts back in.
8. **The ladder cannot lie.** `DeploymentLadder` takes named stages and has no percentage prop.

## Not in Phase 2

No product pages are migrated, no route is redesigned, and nothing connects to a backend.
That is Phase 3 and later.

Phase 2 of the portal redesign is built and runs at **`/opt/nxeon-designsystem`**, a NEW tree —
deliberately not `/opt/nxeon-sandbox`, because that one carries a `.env` and the Phase 2 brief
forbids production credentials.

- Start: `cd /opt/nxeon-designsystem && npm run dev` (or `npx next start -p 3010`) → `/design`
- Port 3010. Prod is 3000, staging 3001, old sandbox 3002.
- Dependencies are exactly next + react + react-dom. No `.env`, no Prisma/DB, no Stripe/registrar/

  addresses from RFC 5737 documentation ranges.
- Next pinned to 15.5.x on purpose (prod is Next 15) so components drop in later without a major-version jump.
- NOT wired to nginx and NOT given a systemd unit — deliberately, to avoid touching prod infra.

Built: tokens in `app/globals.css`; 60-icon family; four surface archetypes (Object with the notch +
status filament, Container, Plate, labelled Rule); controls, navigation, overlays, data, states;
the AppShell; and a showcase at `/design` that navigates via the real shell.

**Why the notch and filament matter:** they belong only to the Object archetype, so "a thing you own"
reads without a label — that is the fix for one card class being used 314 times for objects and prose alike.

**How to apply in later phases:** never introduce a raw hex or hand-typed font size; a border means
"separate object"; one signal colour per view region; violet is reserved for AI/Build only; and
`DeploymentLadder` has no percentage prop by design because the worker reports only six coarse states.

See [[nxeon-portal-redesign-phase1]] for the approved blueprint this implements, and
[[nxeon-pkill-nextstart-incident]] for the operational lesson learned during this phase.

## Later additions (same session)
- **The globe** (`components/system/Globe.tsx`): canvas 2D, no 3D library. ~20k land cells come from
  `/opt/nxeon/public/countries-110m.json` (public-domain Natural Earth 110m), rasterised at BUILD time
  by `scripts/build-land.mjs` into `lib/land.ts` — an 11 KB base64 bitset. Land is projected to unit
  vectors once at mount and only rotated per frame. Great-circle routes carry travelling packets.
  Re-run `node scripts/build-land.mjs` only if the land data changes.
- **The deploy button**: `.nx-deploy` in globals.css is the production `.btn-deploy` hover behaviour
  carried over verbatim (gradient shift, one-shot shimmer sweep, 1px lift, arrow nudge) on the new
  brand ramp. The owner explicitly asked to keep this interaction — do not restyle it.
- **Deployment loaders** (`components/system/DeployLoader.tsx`): five distinct per-product loops —
  vps, game, hosting, domain, email. They LOOP and are never progress; real progress is the
  DeploymentLadder driven by backend states.
- **Glow scale**: `nx-glow-soft` / `nx-glow-card` / `nx-glow-hero` / `nx-lift`. A surface carries at
  most one. Neon stays rationed to a live resource, the brand mark and the primary action.
